records.name: Stormhold
records.held_by: The Vicecanons of Stormhold (the office the city invented); the Hist tree in the town square
records.summary: The province's northern gate and one of its eight great cities: a stone-and-mud city on mounds and ravines beside the river that marks the Morrowind border, built over the Ayleid ruin of Silyanorn around a waterfall. In 4E 201 it is run by Vicecanons and holds the state's customs, its frontier offices and the province's largest and oldest Dunmer minority.

notes.text: Stormhold is the largest settlement of Shadowfen and a major city of Black Marsh, near the banks of the river that forms the border with Morrowind. It is the city of the Valley of Storms and the likeliest first sight of the province for a newcomer.

Barsaebic Ayleids founded Silyanorn here after 1E 198; the Hist later conquered them, by legend. The Dunmer used the site as the foothold of their slave trade, adding stone roads, light posts and bridges and the city invented the Vicecanon office to try slavers. It was the Pact's capital of Black Marsh in 2E, held a prison under Warden Quintus Varus in the late 3E and was overrun but lightly damaged by Umbriel's undead in 4E 48.

The waterfall, the ravine-severed mounds, the Hist in its pond and the Silyanorn substructure all survived 4E 48. The rest has been rebuilt in the 153 years since. Only the population has not recovered. The Vicecanons keep the river customs and the frontier screen's offices here.

Argonians beside the largest and oldest Dunmer minority in Argonia, descended from a colonial population, about a fifth of the city. The western quarter was where the Argonians who worked for the Dunmer lived, and the memory is still live. Townsfolk meet outsiders with pragmatism; they have always had to live with them. Several Vicecanons sit at once, one for each people.

River traffic to Morrowind and to Alten Corimont down the northern trunk road, the customs on that traffic and the Stormhold Crystals dug in the tunnels below. Sedge mats, dried fish and reed goods arrive daily from Jal-Veesa and the weirs; the trading halls sit in the repurposed Ayleid compound.

The Hist tree stands in the town square in the middle of a pond, ringed by ancient pillars and a low stone wall, public and defended. Dunmer households keep their ancestors and a quiet Tribunal-shaped habit; the grave-stake tradition of the Argonians and the Ayleid-compound mortuary sit side by side.

A city on a mountainside: Dunmer ornate stone, stone roads, light posts and long wooden bridges over ravines, with large Argonian mud huts on the mounds between and a waterfall running down through the old Ayleid compound.
Safe inside the walls, where guards keep order. Outside the gate are crocodile-infested ravines and sunken marsh; below the city the Silyanorn tunnels and a sunken Ayleid ruin are an outlaws' refuge.

Below the city, the Silyanorn tunnels hold crystal galleries and an Ayleid well-room that outlaws use as a hideout. The old quarrel between the Argonian west quarter and the Dunmer families flares over a stolen clutch of eggs from the square's Hist pond, and the Vicecanons want the thief found before the quarters settle it themselves.

notes.text: Vandrel Farm is one of the Dunmer-descended smallholdings that ring Stormhold: Stormhold has the oldest Dunmer minority in the province, descended from the colonial slave-trade years and its families farm the raised causeway ground south of the city. One household and two hired hands work a few flooded fields and a stone barn on a mound.
Dunmer-descended farmer, his Argonian wife and children; seasonal Argonian field labour.
Saltrice and eels carried to Stormhold on the causeway; the family pays the causeway toll at the post like any carter.
Ancestor stones by the door and a Hist shoot in a clay pot, the family's one concession to both.
A long stone barn and a two-storey mud-plaster house on a mound ringed by paddy dikes and a stone causeway.
Crocodiles lie in the irrigation ditch. A thief sometimes comes up the valley road at night. Stormhold's patrols ride past the farm.
A missing son who went to the Silyanorn tunnels for crystal; a stranger who asks to rent the barn for a week.

notes.text: Sedgeweir is one of the Veesa-Teeleel fish-weirs that feed Stormhold: the reed-wardens of Jal-Veesa keep the creeks round the city, and the creek south-east of the city is where they set one of their weirs. The name is the wardens' plain word for it.

notes.text: The weirs are older than Stormhold's modern city-state and have been kept by the Sedge-Wardens since before the Dunmer came.

Veesa-Teeleel families on rotation from Jal-Veesa; a weir-warden who knows every trap.
Eels, gar and reed bundles sold up river to Stormhold; weir fees from passing boats.
A small Hist-shoot shrine fed with the first eel of each catch.
Pale stilt huts on a mud bank, a woven fish-weir across the creek, mats and fish drying on racks.
Crocodiles lie around the weir and hackwings swarm over the drying racks in the heat, though the camp itself is safe for the wardens' families.
Someone is pulling up the weir stakes at night and leaving the crocodiles a way in; a boat of Dunmer traders asks to cross without paying.

A timber landing, a rope-hauled flat barge and a long low house of stone and reed.

notes.text: Nenria is a small Barsaebic Ayleid hall in the marsh south of Jal-Veesa. The Barsaebics settled this country after 1E 198 and left halls round Silyanorn and Loriasel; this one stands among them, and its name is of Ayleid shape.
Barsaebic Ayleids settled this country after 1E 198 and were beaten by the Hist, by legend. Of this hall, the wardens know only that their grandmothers ringed it with stakes.
Half-flooded and avoided. The Veesa-Teeleel call it sick ground and keep their own away.
The ruin has no residents; a hermit scavenger sometimes lives there.
Once an outlying hall of the Ayleid settlement; now a source of loot for scavengers.
Ayleid shrine fragments; the Veesa-Teeleel's ward-stakes ring the mound.
White stone arches and fallen columns half-covered with vine on a reed-ringed mound; black water in the undercroft.

The flooded undercroft is the danger: giant snakes lie in the drowned cellar and Ayleid dead stand at the broken arch. The mound top is open ground, and the way in from the Urvyn Farm side is the dry one.
A Welkynd stone that lights by itself in the undercroft; ward-stakes pulled up one by one, and a Jal-Veesa youth seen near the mound at dusk.

Once a waystation for the Legion's couriers; now stripped of any metal.

A low stone wall and arch in a field of reeds; a plinth with a worn Imperial eagle.
Wildlife and the odd thief lurk in the reeds around the ruin. Hackwings swarm over the mud in the heat.
A hoard hidden in the plinth by a Legion courier; a scavenger who wants a witness.

records.name: Karsh-Naal Camp
records.held_by: A band of tribeless Naga
records.summary: A Naga camp in the marsh south of Stormhold, where the brigands of the road-sides live between raids.

notes.text: Karsh-Naal Camp is a Naga brigands' camp in the marsh south of Stormhold. The Naga are the tribeless Argonians of canon who rob travellers on the roads; the busy road from Stormhold toward Helstrom is where such a band would live.

sources.title: Naga highwaymen (Lore:Naga); tribal-camp icon S of Stormhold near the Helstrom road (map)

notes.text: The Naga highwaymen live off the road traffic from Stormhold to Helstrom. They come and go as the merchants do.
A band of Naga lives in huts of woven reed and bone around a fire pit.
Tribeless Naga, tall and hard-eyed and they rob for a living.
Highway robbery and ransom; some trade of stolen goods with Dunmer smugglers.
The Naga worship Sithis at a shrine of bones; no Hist tree stands in the camp.
Reed-and-bone huts around a pit, a lookout on a dead tree and a pole of trophies.
Naga warbands raid from the camp and strike at travellers. The approaches to it are set with traps.
A captive merchant held for ransom; a Naga who wants to defect.

records.name: Slough Point
records.held_by: A council of Lukiul and Nibenese-descended families; Fort Rustmoth's garrison keeps the toll
records.summary: A frontier village at the old border crossing, built round the Imperial census-and-excise post beside a black river whose white bridge has lost its middle span. It lives on the Blackwood Road trade and the toll fort beside it.

notes.text: Slough Point was an Imperial census-and-excise post with a Commission-built white bridge over a black tidal river, its guards chewed by hackwings. It stands inside Black Marsh, beside Fort Rustmoth, close to the Blackwood border.
The Empire built the post, bridge and customs house to tax the Blackwood Road. The Legion left at the secession; the families who served the post stayed on.

A village around the old customs house and the bridge. The bridge's low middle span lies under the black water, and a rope ferry carries the road across. The toll is kept by the garrison of Fort Rustmoth next door.

records.name: Fort Rustmoth
records.held_by: An Archwarden customs garrison keeping the old Imperial fort
records.summary: A stone Imperial keep beside Slough Point, held as the western customs fort on the Blackwood Road. The Imperial eagle still hangs over the gate. It has not been chiselled off.

notes.text: Fort Rustmoth belongs to the Legion's '-moth' series of forts. The Third Empire's Fort Swampmoth stood on the same road between Slough Point and Gideon, and Rustmoth fits that placement and may be the same fort under a later name.
Built by the Third Empire to command the Blackwood Road; not Imperial since the secession, when the Legion left and an ex-Archein family took the keys in the Archwardens' name.
Held, but not by the Empire: an Archwarden garrison charges the road toll and the customs on goods bound for Gideon and Leyawiin, with the old Imperial drill.
Argonian soldiers under an old Archein-lineage captain; a few Nibenese families in the kitchens.
Tolls on the Blackwood Road, a levy on goods bound for Gideon and Leyawiin and fines on smugglers.
No Hist: Imperial foundation. The garrison hatch and bury at village trees.
A square stone keep with corner towers and a yard, the Imperial eagle over the gate, a moat that is now a reed pond.
The fort is guarded and safe inside; wildlife and hackwings are the hazard on the Blackwood Road outside its walls.
A captain who has been paid not to look at a cart; a barracks storeroom short of arrows and armour, and a sergeant who says the captain is selling them to the Sul-Xan.

records.name: Gemin
records.held_by: Wild; haunted; no one holds it
records.summary: The partially flooded, monster-infested ruin of the Conclave of Baal's vaults, north-west of Stormhold, where the tablet that finds Murkwood was kept.

notes.text: The Vaults of Gemin are a ruined structure in Stormhold's city-state that once belonged to the Conclave of Baal. They kept the ancient tablet for deciphering the Elder Scrolls and divining Murkwood's place, and sank into the ground when a spell failed.
The vaults sank when an associate of the Conclave cast a powerful spell. In the Simulacrum the Eternal Champion was sent in to recover the tablet.
A sunk, half-flooded ruin; the Conclave of Baal is long gone from Stormhold, and nobody can locate Murkwood without the tablet.
The vaults have no residents. Treasure-seekers from Stormhold go down into the flooded ruin on their own account.
Once the Conclave's vault; now a source of tablet fragments and relics for scavengers and Stormhold scholars.
The Conclave worshipped learning and bore Molag Bal's name in its title; the Veesa-Teeleel call the ground sick.
A collapsed stone vault entrance in a slope of reeds; half-sunk columns, flooded halls and rune-marked walls.
Undead walk the flooded halls of the sunken vaults, and crocodiles and giant snakes lurk in the water. Rockfall traps are set in the lower halls.
The tablet itself; a Stormhold scholar who needs someone to swim the drowned lowest hall.

terrain_needs.why: the sunk vault entrance cut into a slope

gives.detail: crocodiles and giant snakes in the flooded halls
the vault's warden, a dread wraith

records.name: Loriasel
records.held_by: Wild; lamias and keystone-haunted undead
records.summary: A Barsaebic Ayleid citadel and amphitheatre on a hill over the Venomous Fens, its keystones and its lamia-infested caverns beneath.

notes.text: Loriasel is a ruined Ayleid citadel and amphitheatre built by the Barsaebics for the Ten Ancestors on a hill over the Venomous Fens.

Built after 1E 198 over subjugated Argonians. The Liege Lord bound his knights; the Enchanter turned the binding on him and had the knights kill him. In 2E 582 Dominion soldiers, lamia and ancient Ayleid warriors held it.
The ghost-knights were freed in 2E 582; the Enchanter's works and the keystones remain. The Veesa-Teeleel guard the ruin from looters.
None live here; lamias and undead; a guarded visitor's track from Jal-Veesa.
Once the Ayleid cult centre and keystone workshop; now a source of Ayleid relics, keystone shards and tombs for scavengers.
The Ten Ancestors; a Hist-shoot tended by the Veesa-Teeleel stands outside; Argonians remember the keystones as a theft of their dead.
A hilltop amphitheatre with a ring of ruined seats, an inner bailey and tomb wings below; pale stone and dead trees.
Lamias, undead knights and wards fed by the keystones guard the citadel and the caverns beneath it, making the hill deadly to anyone who enters.
A keystone that still holds a soul; the Hist-shoot outside and its keeper; a looter band that went into the caverns and has not come out.

records.name: Gandranen
records.held_by: Wild; the Fenlord's undead guards and the library's own magic
records.summary: A Barsaebic Ayleid ruin in the fetid mires, with a book-drawing magical library, built by a sorceress of Hermaeus Mora and the tomb of a Fenlord.

notes.text: Gandranen is a Barsaebic Ayleid ruin in Shadowfen: a library of magical halls that draws books from any time, and a Fenlord's tomb crawling with undead slave-guardians.
Built by a sorceress of Hermaeus Mora to attract books; the halls drew in The Lusty Argonian Maid and Ruminations on the Elder Scrolls. Zahra entered about 2E 582 to find the Crown of Ascension.
Volumes still turn up on its shelves; the Fenlord's undead guards still walk the tomb.
The ruin has no residents. An occasional scholar comes to the library, while the Fenlord's undead keep the tomb.
Once a library and tomb; now a treasure for scholars and thieves.
Hermaeus Mora and the Fenlord's death-cult; the Veesa-Teeleel avoid it.
A half-sunk pale-stone ruin on a reed island among black water; shelf-lined halls in the dry part.
The Fenlord's undead slave-guardians walk the tomb halls. The library's own wards guard its shelves.
A book that should not exist in the library; the Fenlord's vault.

records.held_by: Wild; scavengers

notes.text: Agia Nero is a Third Empire road post on the high ground west of Loriasel, on the Gideon-Stormhold way. The Empire held that road with posts and forts until the secession; this one was never re-held, as the Archwardens keep only the forts on the trunk routes.

sources.title: Imperial-ruin icon W of Loriasel on high ground

notes.text: An Imperial road post of the Third Empire, empty since the Legion left at the secession.
Roofless walls, a tower stump and a yard of tall reeds; a scavenger camp in the corner.
The ruin has no residents. Scavengers and smugglers shelter in the broken walls, with a scavenger camp in one corner of the yard.
Once a road post on the Gideon-Stormhold way, it is now stripped of anything of value and offers only shelter.
No Hist shoot grows at this Imperial post; only a worn plinth is left of its shrine.
A broken stone wall, a stump of a tower and an archway half-buried in mud.
Wildlife and the odd thief are the dangers of the ruin, which stands on high ground west of Loriasel.
A smuggler's cache under the tower; a Khajiit runner who hid moon sugar in the wall and wants it back.

records.held_by: Wild; the Veesa-Teeleel keep watch from afar
records.summary: A small Barsaebic ayleid ruin on a sedge island east of Loriasel, with white arches in the reeds and a flooded undercroft.

notes.text: Mirasel is a Barsaebic Ayleid hall on a sedge island east of Loriasel, one of the small halls that ringed the Barsaebic citadel; its name is the Ayleid form of Loriasel's.

sources.title: Ayleid-ruin icon E of Loriasel, on water

notes.text: Mirasel is a small Barsaebic Ayleid hall on a sedge island east of Loriasel, from the settlement that grew in the region after 1E 198. The weir-wardens say it fell with Loriasel.
The island is half-flooded and the Veesa-Teeleel of Reed-Sill Weir, a few cells to the north-east, will not go onto it and tell visitors it is sick ground.
Mirasel has no residents. Weir-wardens from Reed-Sill and Teel-Fen see its white arches on their rounds and have never seen a visitor stay.
It was a minor hall of the Ayleid settlement. Scavengers and relic-hunters now come from Jal-Veesa by the Teel-Fen creek.
A worn Ayleid altar sits under a vine on the island's crown, ringed by Veesa-Teeleel ward-stakes set facing in.
White arches stand in sedge with a fallen column lying across a black pool; the undercroft stairs go down into the water.
Giant snakes in the reeds and undead guardians below the arch; the undercroft stairs go down under black water.
A Jal-Veesa relic-seller will pay for the altar's Welkynd stone, and a Teel-Fen warden says a ward-stake on the west side has been pulled.

records.held_by: Wild; the Veesa-Teeleel keep watch from afar
records.summary: A small Barsaebic Ayleid ruin on the high ground north-west of Slough Point, with white arches in the reeds and a flooded undercroft.

notes.text: Orimel is a small Barsaebic Ayleid hall on high ground north-west of Slough Point. Canon has the Barsaebics holding parts of Blackwood, so their halls reach this far west; the name is in the Ayleid manner.

sources.title: Ayleid-ruin icon NW of Slough Point on high ground

notes.text: Orimel is a small Barsaebic Ayleid hall on high ground north-west of Slough Point, one of the settlements left by the Ayleids after 1E 198. Nobody living can say who built it or how it fell.
The mound's lower rooms stand in black water; Vel-Sapha Stand's people watch it from the track and the Veesa-Teeleel call it sick ground.
Orimel has no residents. Hunters from Vel-Sapha Stand and the Fort Rustmoth garrison patrol the track below it. Neither side goes up.
It was a small Ayleid hall. Relic-hunters from Slough Point now come to it, with the odd Fort Rustmoth soldier looking for white stone.
A cracked Ayleid shrine-stone stands at the top of the mound with Veesa-Teeleel ward-stakes ringed at its foot, leaning in.
White arches rise from the reeds on the high ground, with vines over the fallen columns and black water in the lower rooms. The Rustmoth track runs below.
Undead guardians in the arch and snakes in the reed edge. The lower rooms are flooded and the track below is the only safe ground.
A Vel-Sapha hunter has a carved stone from the shrine he wants rid of, and a Fort Rustmoth sergeant wants to know who keeps re-setting the mound's ward-stakes.

notes.text: Vel-Sapha Stand is a Root-Folk stand round a young Hist at the western edge of Barsaebica. The Root-Folk of Helstrom carry sap and eggs to new trees, and a Hist that rose far from the others would draw a few of them to tend it; the name is in their tongue.

Root-Folk of the Saxhleel tend the stand, sap-gatherers who came from the interior swamp.

Root-hollows and stilt huts sit under a thick canopy on the Barsaebica edge.

The sapling at the heart of the stand is dying. The Root-Folk offer an invitation to the Root Talk.

A Dunmer-descended farmer and his Argonian wife of the Urvyn family keep the farm.
The farm sends saltrice and eels to Stormhold along the northern road.
Ancestor stones from the Dunmer side of the family stand by the house, beside a Hist shoot from the Argonian side.
A stone barn and a stone house stand on a mound that lifts the farm above the flooded fields.
Wildlife in the ditches and fields is the only danger at this quiet farm.
A traveller asks to rent the Urvyns' barn for a few nights, and the Argonian wife has seen him by the Gandranen creek at dusk.

notes.text: Ushaan Camp is a second Naga band's camp, in the marsh south of Gandranen on the road toward Slough Point. Naga rob road traffic, and the Blackwood Road trade passes close by.

notes.text: Naga bands follow road traffic, and this camp south of Gandranen lives off the travellers of the road.
Huts of reed and bone ring a fire pit in the marsh south of Gandranen.
Tribeless Naga, a band of brigands who belong to no clan, hold the camp.

The Naga worship Sithis at a shrine made of bones beside the fire pit, with no Hist tree.
Huts of reed and bone stand around the fire, and a pole hung with trophies marks the camp.

records.summary: A river village at the empty stone chapel of the Maran mission, in the far west. Its people live around a church that the swamp overgrew two centuries ago.

notes.text: Umpholo is the site of a Temple of Mara built about 3E 378. The missionaries died of swamp rot within a month and the library was picked clean by about 3E 399. The story is told in The Argonian Account, Book 4. The site lies in the far west.
The Maran mission's temple was built about 3E 378 and abandoned within a month; the Agaceph looted its books by about 3E 399.
A hamlet of river Argonians living in and around the stripped stone chapel, which the swamp has been overgrowing for two centuries. A fish-and-reed trade with Slough Point.

records.name: Hutan-Aru
records.held_by: The Hutan-Tzel under an elder styled naheesh
records.summary: A fortified outpost of the Hutan-Tzel on a river branch in the far west, one of a chain along the river.

notes.text: Hutan-Aru is a Hutan-Tzel palisade on a river branch in the far west. The spine sets the Hutan-Tzel as river-folk of Blackwood who hold the crossings, and this palisade on the branch is one of their posts; the name is in their style.

sources.title: Hutan-Tzel river-folk of Blackwood (spine §10.2); outpost on a river branch in the far west (map)
outpost icon on a river branch in the far west

notes.text: The Hutan-Tzel hold a chain of river outposts in the far west and have held them for generations; Hutan-Aru is one link.
A palisade of dark posts surrounds a few huts, with a totem carved in runes standing inside.
Hutan-Tzel guards live at the outpost under a local naheesh, an elder of the tribe.

Hutan-Aru's people hunt and guide travellers across the river branch, and sell hides and smoked fish to Umpholo and the Naka-Desh who come to Meliton. They bargain hard over bridge-tolls, which every passing caravan must pay.
The Hutan-Tzel carve their totems with runes that only they can read.
A palisade of dark posts encloses a rune-carved totem and a few huts, with a landing on the river branch.
The Hutan-Tzel say beasts come for anyone who touches a totem, so strangers keep their hands off the carvings.
A traveller can bargain here for passage. One of the totems has been defaced.

gives.detail: a Hutan-Tzel hunter buying hides and meat
Adept Archery trainer, the naheesh's best hunter

records.name: Hutan-Veel
records.held_by: The Hutan-Tzel under an elder styled naheesh
records.summary: A second Hutan-Tzel palisade outpost, far west, on the edge of the Cyrodiil border.

notes.text: Hutan-Veel is the Hutan-Tzel post closest to the Cyrodiil border, where the tribe deals with Cyrodiilic traders at its gate rather than let them into the marsh.

sources.title: Hutan-Tzel of Blackwood (spine §10.2); Cyrodiilic traders on the Blackwood Road (spine §10.3); outpost at the far-west border (map)
outpost icon on the Cyrodiil border

notes.text: Another link in the Hutan-Tzel chain of river outposts, standing on the far-west edge by the Cyrodiil border.
A palisade of dark posts holds a rune-carved totem on the Cyrodiil border.
Hutan-Tzel guards live at the outpost under the elder styled naheesh.

Its people earn their living on the far-west border road: guiding, selling meat to Nahk-Zeel Station and bargaining at the palisade gate with Cyrodiilic traders. The outpost lives on a toll paid in salt.
The guards carve their totems with runes that outsiders cannot read.
A dark palisade stands above a landing at the far-west edge of the marsh.
The guards say beasts follow anyone who disturbs a totem, so the outpost is dangerous to anyone who meddles with its runes.
A traveller disappeared from the far side of the camp. He has not been found.

gives.detail: the gate-keeper, buying hides and meat
Journeyman Sneak trainer, a border scout

records.name: Aldanus Watchtower
records.held_by: Wild
records.summary: A ruined Imperial watchtower on the border hills in the far west.

notes.text: Aldanus Watchtower is a Third Empire watchtower on the border hills above the Blackwood Road. The Empire watched the road to Leyawiin until the secession, and no one re-held a tower so far from the trunk routes.

sources.title: Imperial-ruin icon on the far-west hills

notes.text: Built by the Third Empire to watch the border hills in the far west, and left to fall when the Legion marched out at the secession.
A stump of a tower and a length of wall stand in a thicket on the border hills.
Aldanus Watchtower has no residents. Hutan-Veel scouts climb it for the view and sleep rough in its yard when they range south.
Once a border watch of the Empire, the tower is now stripped of anything useful.
A small shrine niche of the Divines is cut into the tower base, empty now. The Hutan-Tzel do not touch it.
A broken tower and a wall stand in a thicket on the far-west hills.
Wildlife is the main danger in the thicket around the ruined tower.
A Legion courier's bones lie in the rubble at the tower's foot, still wearing an officer's silver ring.

gives.detail: a hackwing nesting on the tower stump

records.name: Meliton
records.held_by: Wild; the Naka-Desh visit to hang chimes
records.summary: A dead Kothringi town of cairns and stone footings in the western hills, left empty since the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560.

notes.text: Meliton is a Kothringi town in the western hills, named like Korydon and Toklea. Canon makes this Blackwood country the Kothringi homeland, which the Knahaten Flu emptied by 2E 603; the ruin above Hutan-Aru is one of those towns.
Meliton was a Kothringi town in the western hills that the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560 left empty, part of a homeland that once held many such towns. The dead were laid in the cairns outside it.
Cairns, footings and two standing walls on a hill-shoulder above Hutan-Aru, where Naka-Desh come now and then to hang chimes for the dead.
The ruin has no residents. The Naka-Desh come on foot from the west, and Hutan-Aru hunters leave them alone.
Once a craft town of glass beads and moonstone. Treasure-diggers now work it, as do the Sul-Xan raiders who come for the cairns.
The Kothringi honoured Z'en, Dibella, Mara and Kynareth and their cairns still hold bead strings. Naka-Desh chimes hang in a single thorn tree beside the largest cairn.
Rings of stone footings on a hill, cairns heaped with glass beads and a chime-hung thorn tree at the centre. Hutan-Aru's smoke shows to the north.
Restless dead rise from the oldest cairns, and Sul-Xan diggers work the south side by day.
A cairn with a humming doll the Naka-Desh will not discuss, and a Sul-Xan trench a Hutan-Aru elder wants filled.

restless Kothringi dead at the cairns

records.name: Aithros
records.held_by: Wild; the Naka-Desh visit to hang chimes
records.summary: Aithros is a dead Kothringi town of cairns and stone footings above a stream, a day south-west of Hutan-Veel near the Cyrodiil border. The Knahaten Flu of 2E 560 emptied it.

notes.text: Aithros is a Kothringi town near the Cyrodiil border, one of the homeland's towns the Flu left empty. Its four cairns for Z'en, Dibella, Mara and Kynareth follow the Kothringi faith canon gives.

sources.title: Kothringi-ruin icon near the Cyrodiil border

notes.text: Aithros was a Kothringi town in the far western hills, emptied by the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560 and never resettled. It lies a day south-west of Hutan-Veel, close to the Cyrodiil border.
Footings, cairns and a few walls above a stream; small Naka-Desh parties come from the border road to hang chimes.
The ruin has no residents. Naka-Desh come in small parties and Hixinoag villagers cut wood on the slope below without crossing it.
It was a craft town with beadwork and a pottery lane. Treasure-diggers and Cyrodilic relic-buyers from Nahk-Zeel Station now visit it.
The Kothringi's four powers are marked by four small cairns at the town's centre, each with a different colour of glass. Naka-Desh chimes hang from one tin frame.
Stone footings in a loose ring around four coloured cairns, with a tin chime-frame and a pottery heap by the stream. The border road is a day to the north.
Restless dead at the four cairns, and Sul-Xan raiders camped in a trench on the stream side.
A pottery heap with unbroken Kothringi bowls that a Nahk-Zeel buyer pays well for, and a raider who left his tools in the trench.

records.name: Anutasil
records.held_by: Wild
records.summary: A small Barsaebic ayleid ruin in the western marsh, white arches in the reeds.

notes.text: Anutasil is a Barsaebic Ayleid hall in the western marsh, the furthest west of their halls in the province. Canon has the Barsaebics holding parts of Blackwood after 1E 198; the name is of Ayleid form.

sources.title: Ayleid-ruin icon in the western marsh

notes.text: Barsaebic Ayleids reached Blackwood after 1E 198, and Anutasil is one of the halls they left in the western marsh.
The ruin in the western marsh is half-flooded and avoided by everyone nearby.
Anutasil has no residents. Umpholo reed-cutters see its arches from their flats and keep clear, and the odd Meliton-bound traveller sleeps in its dry corner.
Once an Ayleid hall, it now stands unused and half-flooded in the reeds.
Fragments of an Ayleid shrine lie among the fallen arches and the vines.
White arches stand half-covered in vine above black water in the western marsh.
Undead guardians and giant snakes make the flooded ruin dangerous.
Umpholo reed-cutters say a white light moves in the flooded hall at night, and a Welkynd stone lies on the stair below the water.
